name: Tamaryokucha

origin.regionNote: Kyushu (Saga, Nagasaki, Kumamoto, Miyazaki as well as Kagoshima)

pluckStandard: steamed or pan-fired, then rolled into curls not needles

processing.description: Two families: mushi-sei (steamed) and kama-iri (pan-fired) tamaryokucha.
Final roll is a comma-shaped curl, not sencha’s needle — export history toward the continent.

aroma: steamed: sencha-like; pan-fired: chestnut and toast
taste: mellow green, often less sharp than Shizuoka sencha

gongfu.curveException: Japanese greens go long–short–long: the first cool steep needs time, the second is quick because the leaf is open, the third lengthens again.

water.note: Soft, 70–80 °C. Kamairi lots can take a little more heat.

storage: Fridge for steamed; pan-fired keeps slightly longer.

shelfLife.note: Sealed, freezer then fridge, small portions.

summary: Kyushu curled green: sencha’s cousin with optional pan-fire chestnut, shaped for a different market.
